title: Strategy — Beginner
summary: An RTS loop: selection and orders, a supplies stock, fog of war, neutral camps, medals, and a save that lets fog recompute.

sections.title: Selection and orders
sections.why: IA_Order reaches only the selected unit, through ReceiveOrder.
reading: A strategy order is not a move of every unit on the map. The player selects, which sets Selected on that unit, and IA_Order is the right click. The excerpt branches if (Selected) and then ProcessEvent on ReceiveOrder. A tank and a rifle squad implement the same function. The unselected units do not hear the click. Tick that searches the whole level for the cursor repeats a query the selection already answered.

UE5 selection can be a box trace once, on the press, writing Selected. It is not a per-frame overlap of every unit with the mouse. The order payload, a point or a target, belongs on the interface inputs. This sample calls the function with no parameters, which is the shape to extend, not a reason to move the unit inside the order graph. The unit's own movement consumes the order.

Formations are data on the squad, not a tick that assigns offsets. The economy spends when an order builds something. It does not run inside ReceiveOrder unless the unit's implementation asks it. Fog hides units the player has not seen. An order should not reveal them. Scoring hears a result later. It does not issue orders.
Save stores Selected only if the mode restores a selection. It always stores the order the unit is still executing, or a load resumes idle squads that were mid-march.

sections.title: Supplies
sections.why: Spend subtracts a data cost on the authority.
reading: The strategy economy is a stock of supplies. Spend is a custom event, not Tick. The excerpt assigns Supplies = (Supplies - 25.f) inside if (HasAuthority()). The 25 is the sample cost. A data row should own it, so a barracks and a turret do not share a literal typed in the graph. A client that subtracts outside that check spends a private stock, and the copies diverge.

An order to build calls Spend. ReceiveOrder does not itself subtract, or every move order would bill the player. The unit asks the economy when the order is a purchase. Fog does not spend. Scoring does not. A refund is the same event with a negative cost, still on the authority, still from the data row.

Replicating the coin icon, or every floating number, is the expensive version. The float is the state. The UI binds to it. A Tick that drips income also drips while the match is paused and never asks whether a building exists. Income, if you add it, is a slow timer that calls the same Spend path with a negative cost.
Save stores Supplies after the server write. Loading a client's guess fills the base with money the host did not have.

Supplies closes on Economy. Spend subtracts a data cost on the authority. Line 7 is `if (HasAuthority()) // node:tpl_economy_auth`. Line 9 is `Supplies = (Supplies - 25.f); // node:tpl_economy_set`. Nest Supplies = (Supplies - 25.f) inside HasAuthority. The data row owns the cost. Spend is the event, not Tick. The assignment names the repair to keep. sections.title: Fog of war
sections.why: Reveal runs four times a second. Visible is a team fact.
reading: Fog of war is what this team can see. Begin Play starts Reveal on a 0.25 second looping timer in the excerpt. Reveal traces and, on a hit, assigns Visible = true. A wall blocks the trace. The bool is a team fact. It is not a widget per spectator, and it is not something a client may set to cheat the map. The sample has no authority gate. Add one before you trust the write in a networked match.

Orders must not set Visible. Buying a unit must not. A unit that walks into a cell is why the timer exists. Polling every cell on Tick reveals the whole map's cost every frame, including cells nobody moved through. 0.25 seconds is a vision pass. The replication graph, later, is how far the newly visible unit's actor travels.

The patrol of a neutral camp is hidden while Visible is false. The camp still simulates on the server. The client's UI simply does not draw it. Save may store explored cells if the design remembers the map. It does not need to store the current Visible bit if the timer will recompute it from unit positions after load.
Anti-cheat is the same sentence: clients do not write Visible. They receive it.

sections.title: Neutral camps
sections.why: A camp walks its route on a timer while fog hides it.
reading: A neutral camp is a patrol the player has not ordered. Begin Play sets AdvancePatrol on a 1 second timer. The A path assigns GoingRight = true. The B path is empty, so the camp's return is unfinished. Fog's Visible bit decides whether the client draws the camp. The camp graph does not write Visible, or walking would light the map.

Tick that moves the camp also moves it while the match is paused and spends a path query the timer replaced. The route is data. The player' s IA_Order does not target a camp unless the design says camps can be captured, and then capture is ReceiveOrder on a different selection, not a hijack of this timer.

Scoring does not run when the camp merely turns around. A kill of the camp calls the medal event. Supplies are not spent by a neutral walker. Save can store GoingRight so the camp resumes the same leg. It should not store the mesh.

If the camp is not visible, the server still advances it. Freezing hidden camps makes the map lie the moment the trace reveals them, because they pop at the point they were hidden, not the point they walked to.

sections.title: Medals
sections.why: AwardMedal adds a data value on the authority.
reading: A medal is a result, not an order. AwardMedal is the server event for a kill or an objective. The excerpt assigns Score = (Score + 10.f) inside if (HasAuthority()). Ten is the sample. The data asset should name the medal's value, the way the economy's row names a cost. A client that awards its own medal, outside that check, inflates the board. The board then shows a number the host never granted.

The board widget reads Score. It is not replicated. Fog does not add score when a cell becomes visible. Supplies are not score. Spending and scoring can share the authority habit. They must not share the float, or a purchase lowers the kill board.

The camp patrol does not call AwardMedal when it flips GoingRight. The kill does. An order completed, a point captured, is another call with a different data value. Tick that scans for dead units rediscovers deaths the kill event already reported.
Save stores Score after the server add. A load that adds 10 again because Begin Play fires AwardMedal double-counts the match.

sections.title: Save the match
sections.why: Begin Play restores supplies, score, and the route, then fog recomputes.
reading: The strategy slot packs Supplies, Score, GoingRight for each camp, and the orders units are still executing. It does not pack Visible. The fog timer recomputes vision from positions after load, and a saved Visible bit would show a camp that has since walked. The excerpt assigns SlotValue = 1.f at Begin Play and LoadSlot logs Loaded. That is the pack shape. The struct fields are the ones above.

Tick that writes the slot stores a Spend that has not finished and a score medal that has not been awarded, or awards it twice if you are not careful. Write on the match event that asked for a save. Do not let Begin Play call Spend or AwardMedal. It only reads.

Selection can be dropped. The player reselects. The march order cannot be dropped, or the load shows idle units that should be halfway across the map. Store the order id and the target point. Store the formation id, not every member's offset. The offsets are data.
Apply supplies and score before the UI binds. Start camp timers after GoingRight is set. Start fog after the units are placed, so the first Reveal sees the loaded world.
